claims.reason: `hlen` is an explicit binder of the theorem. Nothing else in the statement mentions it. In the proof it is used only once: in the `omega` step that gets `hi' : i < next.length` from `hi : i < (C.stepOfL Δ).length`. `hi` comes from `hS.nonBasicStep` and does not depend on `hlen`. The bound `hi'` can be derived without `hlen`. `hlab i hi : C.Q.labelAt (x ++ [i]) = some _`. Here `labelAt q y = (q.atOpt y).map label` (QuasiTableau.lean:298). `QuasiTab.atOpt_snoc` (PreInterpolant.lean:202) gives `q.atOpt (x ++ [i]) = (q.atOpt x).bind (fun n => n.children[i]?)`. Rewriting with `hx`, and using `QuasiTab.children (.QNode _ _ next) = next` (QuasiTableau.lean:38, rfl), gives `(next[i]?).map label = some _`. If `next.length ≤ i`, then `next[i]? = none` and the left side is `none`, a contradiction. So `i < next.length`. The library already does this rewrite in `iitpList_getElem_eq_iitp`. The rest of the proof does not use `hlen`, so the theorem stays true and provable after deleting it.
